title: Write a worldview that can be questioned

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A contradiction affirms and denies the same claim under the same conditions. Different levels of explanation can coexist: a person can choose while resources constrain which choices are available. Coherence alone does not establish truth.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional worldview A: reality includes material processes; people can learn; testimony is useful but fallible; promises matter; suffering sometimes has preventable causes; responsibility depends partly on available choices. B shares these positions except that it says every adult always has exactly the same opportunities. Case: two learners can study, but one has an accessible library and the other has no available transport or accessible copy.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Use all six headings to compare A/B. Identify the tension, a strong objection, a justified revision condition and one practical implication. Keep unresolved metaphysical questions unresolved.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A position says testimony is always unreliable but treats one admired speaker’s testimony as conclusive without corroboration. What needs examination, and what would a narrower position allow?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: A can retain agency while recognizing unequal options. B’s equal-opportunity claim conflicts with the stipulated access difference; revise that claim rather than deny the learner’s agency. At a fictional later review an accessible copy arrives but transport remains unavailable: update the particular options, not a universal equality claim. Partial: identify unfairness without locating the proposition. Incorrect: announce all responsibility impossible.
criteria: Contradiction is distinguished from different explanatory levels

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: The exception conflicts with “always” unless independently justified. A narrower view treats testimony as fallible and checks source access, reasons and corroboration. Agreement with the admired speaker does not settle reliability.
criteria: Contradiction is distinguished from different explanatory levels
